candidates.concept: The crossbars of both e's escape their letterforms and run as one thread through the entire word at e-bar height, surfacing as stitch dashes in every gap and counter and passing behind every stem. The e's are structurally pinned to the thread: their bars ARE the thread.

T and h fused into one glyph by a shared crossbar strung from the T stem to the h stem. The span between the two posts sags under its own weight — a thread strung between two points, drawn with the physics of a real line. The h's ascender terminates at the crossbar's underside; cut the ligature and the h is decapitated.

The first e's counter is replaced by a perfect circular eye holding a concentric node — a record pinned in the eye of the needle. The geometric counter against Geist's organic bowls makes the e the focal event of the word.

A single uninterrupted thread enters from the left, ties one knot, and becomes the T's crossbar — the mark and the wordmark are literally the same stroke. The T's left arm is the thread's arrival; delete the mark and the T is broken. The knot is the extractable small-slot mark.

The i's dot becomes the needle's eye: an enlarged node whose thread is drawn entirely in negative space — an unprinted channel enters from the left and terminates in the eye. The line is read in the absence of ink. The node is the extractable mark and the 16px survivor.

candidates.hook: double-l verticals (adjacent d/l ascender pair in 'threadline')
candidates.typeface: Space Grotesk or Sora (OFL alternate, pipeline rerun)
candidates.concept: The d and l ascenders — the word's twin verticals — are shortened and their strokes escape upward into a single connecting arc: one stitch rising out of the fabric of the word and diving back in. The stitch (two posts + arc) is the extractable mark.

candidates.typeface: custom monoline mark + Geist 600 wordmark (Phase 160 kit)
candidates.concept: A single uninterrupted monoline thread writes 'th' — crossbar, stem, baseline turn, rise, shoulder, post — one stroke with two loose ends. The mark leads; the wordmark accompanies on a shared baseline grid. The monogram is the designated 16px silhouette survivor.

candidates.typeface: Space Grotesk Medium (OFL alternate, pipeline rerun, lowercase 'threadline')
candidates.concept: A needle has passed through every vertical stem of the word at one consistent height, leaving a row of punch holes — a repeating pattern through the letterforms. The thread itself is never shown; you see the evidence of its path and follow it. Pure type, no mark.

techniques_twice: Continuous-line mark (C4 T crossbar / C7 Th pair)
